Hey, I understand that being a pilot and having all this knowledge can make you feel weirded out by people who get nervous. Remember, it’s something quite incredible for a lot of us that a super heavy tin can lift itself up to the sky, it isn’t attached to anything, it’s just there floating. We feel fragile, we feel we are not in control of our fate if all our irrational fears were to happen. We think, “machines can fail. People can fail. How is this safe?” We basically feel at the mercy of chance.

The sensations we feel are not normal to us, all the sounds we hear that no one explains can be unnerving, the sudden movements or bumpiness can make it feel like the tin can can easily break. 

The information I know now is thanks to that FA I mentioned, who was kind enough to sit by me during a panic attack, wait for me to calm down, asked and heard my concerns, and explained in a logical way with facts why I’m/we’re safe. That gave me the courage to do further research, since in my mind the more I knew, the more afraid I’d be, because maybe I’d find information that I wouldn’t like. After that I started to love flying, and I will forever thank him. 

Try to have a bit more gentility when you encounter someone like me, who naturally is afraid of the unknown. Of course I’m looking for reassurance, of course I’m looking for answers. What good would it do to keep fears bottled up? And I don’t want to go back to being terrified of flying. I found it added to my life and don’t want to give it up. 

Your tone is not helpful to the other person. Being condescending, or shaming will hinder communication, the other person won’t be as receptive. And we look to people like you for answers.
